run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T07:56:37Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend traces to the frontend's checkout path. From the 5-minute error point at 07:57:37 onward, frontend spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR appear only on POST /api/checkout, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and the client span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (peak ~0.76 errors/s), plus a small tcp.connect error rate; every other frontend route and gRPC dependency stayed at zero errors, and frontend itself is ready with 0 restarts. Checkout stopped serving: its PlaceOrder/HTTP POST span rate fell from ~1.6-1.73/s to 0 by 08:05-08:10 with no checkout span carrying STATUS_CODE_ERROR, the checkout Endpoints object has zero ready addresses (only a notReadyAddresses entry for pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q), and checkout is the only one of 21 otel-demo Deployments with unavailableReplicas 1. That pod is Running but its checkout container is not ready (CrashLoopBackOff, restartCount 11, last termination reason Error, exitCode 2), and its spec container image is gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest while the Deployment template still specifies ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout - the pod was mutated outside the Deployment. chaos-mesh events show Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay spawning a PodChaos every minute from 07:55:30 (one minute before the 07:56:37 alert), each recording 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q' and recovering ~55s later. product-catalog latency stayed flat (p95 ~1.92ms) with a ready pod and 0 restarts, so the 'product-catalog-network-delay' name does not describe what was applied; all flagd fault flags are 'off' and no NetworkPolicy objects exist. The PodChaos specs, failing trace spans and previous-container logs were not available, so the exact chaos action and the origin of exit code 2 remain hypotheses/gaps.

claims.text: Frontend span error rate was 0 for every operation until the 5-minute point at 07:57:37, then became non-zero only on POST /api/checkout, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and the client span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (0.185/s at 07:57:37, rising to 0.72-0.76/s, still 0.37/s at 08:09:37). Frontend tcp.connect error rate became non-zero at the same point (0.033-0.056/s).

Frontend spans for GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST /api/cart, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart had an error rate of exactly 0 at every sampled point while the alert was firing; only the checkout path errored.

The checkout service stopped serving: its span rates for oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and HTTP POST were ~1.6-1.73/s through the 5-minute point covering 07:50-07:55, fell to 0.09/s and 0.27/s at 08:00, and were 0 at 08:05 and 08:10. Every checkout span carried status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET; no checkout span had STATUS_CODE_ERROR, so the failing frontend calls did not reach a checkout server span.

The checkout Endpoints object has zero ready addresses: its only subset entry is notReadyAddresses with targetRef Pod otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q (IP 100.96.4.26) on port 8080, consistent with connection-level (tcp.connect) failures from the frontend to checkout:8080.

Pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q (owner ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb, started 07:18:48) is phase Running but its checkout container is ready=false with waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 2m40s restarting failed container=checkout'), restartCount 11, and lastState terminated reason Error, exitCode 2, startedAt 08:02:25 / finishedAt 08:02:30; pod condition Ready=False (ContainersNotReady) since 08:02:30.

The checkout pod's spec container image is gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest, while the checkout Deployment's pod template still specifies ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout and the container status image references ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:f000c1de37175546a22846714e1c11a19bc2997e8769bb7bffcab5c4c10c24b2; the pod object was therefore mutated outside the Deployment, with no new ReplicaSet replacing it.

checkout is the only degraded workload in otel-demo: Deployment checkout has replicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1 and no readyReplicas, while the other 20 deployments (including frontend, frontend-proxy, product-catalog, payment, cart, currency, shipping, email) each report readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1.

Events on pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q tie its restarts to the alert onset: Killing 'Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted' count 7, first 07:55:30 last 07:58:30; Pulled 'Container image "gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest" already present on machine' count 6, 07:55:30-08:01:57; BackOff 'Back-off restarting failed container checkout in pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q_otel-demo' count 26, 07:57:30-08:03:18.

The chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay is what applied the fault to checkout: it Spawned a new PodChaos every minute (otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-zv9mn 07:55:30, -927gn 07:56:30, -d2m7w 07:57:30, -dc4vz 07:58:30, -jgn2n 07:59:30, -ktl9k 08:00:30, -vxxwz 08:01:30, -6cwbh 08:02:30, -qgddz 08:03:30, -gl228 08:04:30), and each PodChaos recorded Started, then Applied 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q', then TimeUp/'Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q' roughly 55s later.

Checkout's readable container log is normal order-processing output ('[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through', 'order placed', Kafka write success): the newest 120 of 2239 lines read span 07:40:55.508-07:41:39.651 (view reported incomplete on its limit), and no previous container instance was available to read.

product-catalog was healthy throughout: its p95 span duration was flat at 1.92ms (1.916-1.941ms) at every 5-minute point from 07:35 to 08:10, its pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-q8nt8 is ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination, and its Deployment has readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) has defaultVariant 'off' for every fault flag, including adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems and loadGeneratorFloodHomepage.

The NetworkPolicy query for the cluster returned an empty item list (total_items_processed 0), so no NetworkPolicy object was present in what this Run observed to be blocking frontend-to-checkout traffic.

Frontend's own workload was up: Deployment frontend has readyReplicas 1 and availableReplicas 1, and pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-gc9hg is ready with restartCount 0 and no waiting or last-terminated state.

ad and fraud-detection show a pre-existing, tiny error rate on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans (~0.0037/s) present both before and during the alert window (points at 07:45, 08:00, 08:10); this background error is not tied to the frontend checkout failures and is not part of this cause.

Rejected: a network delay on product-catalog (suggested by the chaos object's name 'otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay') was not the fault. product-catalog p95 stayed ~1.92ms, its pod is ready with 0 restarts, it emitted no error spans, and the Applied events name otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9dn2q as the chaos target.

Rejected: a flagd feature-flag fault (e.g. paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, cartFailure) was not the cause. Every flag in flagd-config has defaultVariant 'off', and payment, cart and product-catalog show no error spans and healthy deployments.

Rejected: the frontend itself did not break. Its deployment and pod are ready with 0 restarts, and its errors are confined to the checkout path while every other route and gRPC dependency it calls stayed error-free.

The PodChaos action is likely 'pod-failure': the pod's spec container image was replaced with gcr.io/google-containers/pause:latest and the pod events show 'Container checkout definition changed, will be restarted' plus pause image pulls, which matches Chaos Mesh's pod-failure mechanism. The PodChaos/Schedule specs are not readable, so the declared action, duration and selector remain unverified.

The chaos Schedule's name references product-catalog while its Applied events target the checkout pod, which suggests a misconfigured selector in otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay; its selector and spec could not be read to confirm this.

The checkout container's 'Error' termination with exitCode 2 (08:02:25-08:02:30) could reflect the kubelet killing the container when the chaos image swap is applied/reverted, or a checkout startup failure of its own; the previous container instance's logs were unavailable, so this is not resolved.

Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and the PodChaos objects it spawns, confirm the action (likely pod-failure) and its selector, and suspend or delete the experiment if the checkout outage is not intended; if a product-catalog network delay was intended, correct the selector.

After the chaos experiment is stopped, verify the checkout pod's spec image returns to ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout, its container becomes Ready, the checkout Endpoints object regains a ready address, and frontend POST /api/checkout errors return to 0.

gaps: The chaos-mesh Schedule and PodChaos custom resources could not be read (those kinds are not exposed by the tools), so the experiment's declared action, duration, selector and whether it is still active are unverified; attribution to the Schedule rests on chaos-mesh events.

The alerting rule query for 'RequestErrorRate' returned no_data (e490f9eb-8739-4aa4-b05b-9e61588a8fe1-t0:65933aa1-9aa1-484a-b498-9ec188628d5c), so the alert's exact expression, window and threshold are unknown.

Jaeger trace searches returned no_data for the incident window (ec81e440-dc96-44df-a836-46505173f4e4-t0:170b6c3a-2e33-4ae6-be7d-af3329a0dd29 and 89838ba9-aa12-4cd3-b6a0-c624a27f004f-t1:9e478d11-ae72-4cf3-8dd3-791ab5de8ccb); the traces that were returned were pre-incident (07:49:32-07:49:33, all 200 / grpc status 0) and incomplete, so the failing spans' status tags and error details could not be inspected.

The rpc client/server duration queries returned no_data (c3163661-07de-4711-afe5-5f0d62bc8385-t1:b522b438-f421-4258-a4f2-088126cd74c8, 276b1c71-4872-4eb2-82f0-0fd6a8460153-t0:15bd18e6-8c59-4a5e-aabe-ab56aed7a740), so no gRPC status-code breakdown was available.
The checkout container's previous instance logs were unavailable ('previous terminated container ... not found'), so the cause of the exitCode 2 'Error' termination could not be confirmed.

Frontend pod log reads returned no_data (45257464-93a7-4f1d-94e2-3b45437372b9-t0:1ccd6595-ec98-4de4-8fc1-091a4d9b870c and b49d3509-f8ef-42bc-95e3-d795b5db95c7-t0:b789aa33-a9aa-4ea3-ab5a-1788bc94eac2), so the frontend's own client-side error text for the failed checkout calls is unknown.

The kube_pod_container_info query returned no_data (ed455608-7c90-410d-97b3-8394fb54f8ad-t0:c6445866-3a68-4fcb-a616-20f9aa56eb56), so no Prometheus view of pod container images corroborates the pause-image substitution.

The checkout pod's spec image (pause:latest) and crash state were observed only at query time (~08:15); the timing of each individual image swap was inferred from events rather than observed directly.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change history could be checked.
next_steps: Have the platform owner read the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay and its PodChaos children (spec.action, duration, selector, mode) to confirm the pod-failure targeting of the checkout pod and decide whether to suspend it.
Once the experiment is stopped, confirm checkout returns to Ready and the checkout Service regains a ready endpoint, then confirm frontend POST /api/checkout errors return to zero.

Retrieve the checkout container's previous-instance logs from the node, or re-run with longer log retention, to determine whether exitCode 2 came from the application or from the chaos-driven restarts.
